# 1 Samuel Chapter 23 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 164r–164v | **Source Image:** 1SA_023_page_001.jpg, 1SA_023_page_002.jpg

---

**1** David was told, "The Philistines are attacking Keilah and looting the threshing floors."

**2** David asked the LORD, "Should I go and fight these Philistines?" The LORD answered, "Go, attack the Philistines and rescue Keilah."

**3** But David's men said to him, "We're already afraid here in Judah. How much worse if we go to Keilah and face the Philistine army!"

**4** So David asked the LORD again, and the LORD answered, "Go down to Keilah. I am handing the Philistines over to you."

**5** David and his men went to Keilah and fought the Philistines. He drove off their livestock and inflicted heavy losses on them. David saved the people of Keilah.

**6** When Abiathar son of Ahimelech had fled to David at Keilah, he brought the ephod with him.

**7** When Saul was told that David had gone to Keilah, he said, "God has handed him over to me! He has trapped himself by entering a town with gates and bars."

**8** Saul called up all his forces for war, to march down to Keilah and besiege David and his men.

**9** David learned that Saul was plotting against him. He said to Abiathar the priest, "Bring the ephod."

**10** Then David prayed, "LORD, God of Israel, your servant has heard that Saul plans to come to Keilah and destroy the town because of me.

**11** Will the leaders of Keilah hand me over to him? Will Saul actually come, as your servant has heard? LORD, God of Israel, tell your servant." The LORD said, "He will come."

**12** David asked, "Will the leaders of Keilah hand me and my men over to Saul?" The LORD said, "They will."

**13** So David and his men — about six hundred of them — left Keilah and kept moving from place to place. When Saul heard that David had escaped from Keilah, he called off the campaign.

**14** David stayed in the wilderness strongholds, in the hill country of the Ziph wilderness. Saul searched for him every day, but God did not let him be found.

**15** While David was at Horesh in the wilderness of Ziph, he learned that Saul had set out to kill him.

**16** Jonathan, Saul's son, went to David at Horesh and helped him find strength in God.

**17** "Don't be afraid," Jonathan told him. "My father Saul will never lay a hand on you. You will be king over Israel, and I will be your second-in-command. Even my father knows this."

**18** The two of them made a covenant before the LORD. David stayed at Horesh, and Jonathan went home.

**19** The Ziphites went to Saul at Gibeah and said, "David is hiding among us in the strongholds at Horesh, on the hill of Hachilah south of the wasteland.

**20** Whenever you want to come down, O king, come — and we will hand him over to you ourselves."

**21** Saul replied, "The LORD bless you for caring about me.

**22** Go and make sure. Find out exactly where he goes and who has seen him there, because I'm told he is very cunning.

**23** Find every hiding place he uses, and come back to me with reliable information. Then I'll go with you. If he's anywhere in the land, I'll track him down among all the clans of Judah."

**24** So the Ziphites left for Ziph ahead of Saul. Meanwhile, David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, in the Arabah south of the wasteland.

**25** Saul and his men went to search for him. When David heard about it, he moved down to the rock formation and stayed in the wilderness of Maon. When Saul heard this, he pursued David there.

**26** Saul was going along one side of the mountain, and David and his men along the other. David was racing to get away, while Saul's forces were closing in to capture them.

**27** Then a messenger came to Saul: "Come quickly! The Philistines are raiding the land!"

**28** Saul broke off his pursuit of David and went to deal with the Philistines. That is why the place is called the Rock of Escape.

**29** David went up from there and took refuge in the strongholds of En-gedi.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

1. **23:7 — "God has handed him over"**: Saul reads providence backward. He sees David's entry into a walled town as divine entrapment — but it is Saul who misreads every sign. David consults God through the ephod; Saul imposes his own interpretation on events.

2. **23:11-12 — the ephod oracle**: This is the clearest window into how binary divination worked in ancient Israel. David asks two yes/no questions; the LORD answers both. The answers are devastating — yes, Saul will come; yes, the people David just saved will betray him. Gratitude has limits.

3. **23:16-18 — Jonathan's last visit**: This is the last time Jonathan and David will ever meet. Jonathan crosses enemy lines to strengthen his friend — and to formally yield his crown. "I will be your second-in-command" is the most selfless political statement in the Hebrew Bible. They make a covenant, and Jonathan walks out of the story.

4. **23:26-28 — the Rock of Escape**: The most cinematic moment in the fugitive narrative. Saul's forces are literally closing the circle when a messenger arrives with news of a Philistine raid. David escapes by seconds. The narrator names the rock to memorialize the moment — and the invisible providence behind it.

— PNEUMA
